tool_input.message:
Local code review on `3cf6bf4` (requirement 1) came back: 6 findings, all Important, none Critical. Core match-and-consume logic verified CORRECT — the reviewer traced every exit path and confirmed `onDispatched` fires strictly after the encode, so "blocked or encode-failed spawn does not consume" holds as written. Claim-vs-dispatch asymmetry also verified clean.

Fold these into `m-2026-09-08-004` alongside the requirement-2 work; two of them touch files you're already in. Two more local reviewers are still running — I'll forward anything they add rather than making you wait.

**F1 — the MCP twin of the fixed CLI path was never updated (`internal/mcp/mission_tools.go`), confidence 88.** `handleCreateMission` writes the identical `BindOriginDispatch` sidecar via its own `bindDispatchedMission` (:205), documented as mirroring `cmd/ethos/mission.go`. You fixed the CLI string; this one still promises unscoped capture. Three sites: `:160` and `:187` doc comments ("the very next `Agent()` spawn ... writes its delegation under whatever mission the sidecar named"), and `:259`, an operator-facing string returned to MCP clients. Also a parity gap: the CLI now prints the binding unconditionally and names the Worker; MCP emits nothing on a fresh bind, so an MCP-driven leader never learns the binding is worker-scoped. Mirror the CLI wording and add the worker to the fresh-bind output. `format_output.go` is in your write-set if a formatter is implicated (DES-020).

**F2 — `spawnAgentType`'s doc comment claims a sharing that does not exist, confidence 92.** `pretooluse_dispatch.go:80-82` says it is "shared by ... `readActiveMissionForDispatch` and `dispatchTierB`'s own delegation-skeleton write, so both see the same answer." `dispatchTierB` never calls it — `:436-439` is a verbatim inline copy. You deduped the identical block in `pretooluse_inherit.go:261` and missed the one in the same file. No behavioral difference today, but the stated guarantee rests on two copies staying in sync, which is precisely what extracting the helper was meant to prevent. Replace `:436-439` with a call.

**F3 — the mismatch warning prints `worker ""` on a contract-load failure without saying so, confidence 87.** `pretooluse_dispatch.go:154-161`. `dispatchedWorker` returns `("", false)` on any Load failure, so the operator sees `bound to m-X for worker ""` — and `validate.go:182` makes worker mandatory non-empty, so an empty worker there can ONLY mean the contract would not load. DES-076 devotes a whole bullet to that case being a deliberate doctrine divergence, and then it fires invisibly. Branch on `ok` and emit a distinct line naming the load failure. This is the finding I care most about after F6: a documented divergence that is unobservable when it happens is not actually documented.

**F4 — `consumeDispatchBinding`'s failure-mode comment understates the degradation, confidence 85.** `:188-190` claims a failure "degrades the fix to 'capture at most one more spawn'." Under a persistent clear failure (EACCES, read-only mount) the sidecar survives every attempt, so every subsequent matching-worker spawn is captured — unbounded, not one. Still better than pre-fix, but state the real bound.

**F5 — DES-076's contract-load-failure decision has no test, confidence 85.** The only malformed-sidecar test (`pretooluse_test.go:2301`) uses a CLAIM-origin sidecar and asserts deny — the opposite branch. A regression that made the dispatch path block on an unresolvable contract passes the entire suite. Add the dispatch-origin case: nonexistent mission, assert allow, empty `MISSION_ID`, sidecar intact. The ADR's Tests section lists three tests and does not admit this gap; fix that too.

**F6 — a partially-failed `ClearActiveMission` degrades a dispatch binding into a sticky claim, confidence 80. Read this one carefully; it resurrects the bug you just fixed.** `internal/mission/active.go:341-344` uses `errors.Join(removeSidecarFile(active), removeSidecarFile(origin))`, which evaluates both unconditionally. If the active-mission removal fails and the origin removal succeeds, the surviving state is active-mission present / origin absent — which `ReadActiveMissionBinding:137` reads as `BindOriginClaim`: sticky, ungated by agent type, stamping commit trailers. The function's own comment claims "a half-cleared pair converges"; this half-cleared pair converges to the wrong answer. Pre-existing, but newly reachable from your consume path and newly consequential. Only attempt the origin removal when the active-mission removal succeeded — and fix the comment's claim while you are there.

Related test gap the reviewer flagged with F6: `..._MismatchedWorkerNotCaptured` asserts only `ReadActiveMission == missionID`. If a future change dropped the origin file while leaving active-mission, the binding would silently degrade to a sticky claim and the test would still pass. Assert `ReadActiveMissionBinding` and check `Origin == BindOriginDispatch`.

**Housekeeping:** `internal/hook/zz_probe_test.go` was left untracked in the worktree and fails `make check` on gofmt. The reviewer moved it to `.tmp/zz_probe_test.go.bak` rather than deleting it. I assume it was red-first probe scaffolding from round 1 — retrieve it if you still need it, but scratch files belong in `.tmp/`, not in a package directory where they enter the lint set.

Your `8536df0` looks right to me on read: closed provenance enum, empty string never treated as evidence, three mechanical checks, no bypass flag, gate 2 untouched, backward compat pinned against a real on-disk record. I have not seen a CHANGELOG entry yet — the contract requires one under `[Unreleased]`.
